items.finding: createRun ran outside the transaction holding the gate, so the run row was not atomic with the decision and a job could never be enqueued in the same commit (ADR-0004's transactional enqueue).
items.fix: fixed: acquire passes the transaction to createRun through a narrow TxClient, and the lock test inserts on it

items.finding: The Lock interface exposed lockKey, a Postgres advisory-lock concept, on a seam meant to be swappable for NATS.
items.fix: fixed: lockKey is off the interface and stays a standalone export

items.finding: The plan promised reconnect, but a dropped connection only cleared the client; a live subscriber went deaf until something else called subscribe or publish.
items.fix: fixed: the bus reconnects with backoff and re-issues LISTEN for every channel that still has a handler, proved by a test that terminates the backend and publishes again

items.finding: The index title did not match the ADR's own heading.
§4 still says the worker releases the lock, which ADR-0016 reinterprets.
items.fix: answered: follow-up recorded; architecture.md is outside this unit

items.finding: The DoD said 'after its expiry' but the test drives retry delay, a different pg-boss mechanism.
items.fix: fixed: the DoD now says retry delay, which is what is tested

items.finding: retryLimit defaulted to a bare 3 while the other defaults were named constants.
ensureQueue swallowed every error, hiding a real connectivity or permission failure.
items.fix: fixed: only an already-exists error is swallowed, anything else is rethrown

summary: ADR-0016 soundly resolves the ADR-0004 and architecture §4 contradiction and is verified by lock.test.ts; the bus, queue and cache match ADR-0004's pointer, pg-boss-schema and unlogged-shared-truth requirements with injection-safe channel handling; control still imports only the kernel.
